html:
Humberstone and Santa Laura are two abandoned nitrate towns in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, now a World Heritage Site. They are relics of the nitrate boom that made Chile rich from the 1880s to the 1920s.

Sodium nitrate, mined from the desert crust, was the world's main fertiliser and an ingredient of explosives. After the War of the Pacific, Chile controlled almost the whole world supply. British and Chilean companies built hundreds of works, where miners from the south, Bolivia and Peru lived in company towns and were paid in tokens. Export taxes paid for most of the state's budget.

Strikes were met with force; at Iquique in 1907 soldiers killed hundreds of strikers and their families in the Santa María School massacre. After German chemists learned to make nitrate from the air, demand collapsed, and the towns emptied. Copper took nitrate's place.
